title: How a Chainsaw Works in 60 Seconds 🪵⚙️ #shorts
description:
A chainsaw is a tiny one-cylinder engine driving a loop of about 30 hardened steel teeth around a long guide bar. A centrifugal clutch keeps the chain still at idle and grabs only when the engine revs up, and oil keeps the chain sliding while it chews through wood. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#chainsaw #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A chainsaw is a *saw blade* with no ends, a loop of about *30 steel teeth*.

steps.label: Engine
steps.text: Inside sits a tiny *one-cylinder* engine, often a two-stroke, revving thousands of times a minute.

steps.label: Clutch
steps.text: At idle, the chain stays still. Rev up, and *spinning weights* fly outward and grab the *clutch drum*.

steps.label: Sprocket
steps.text: The drum turns a *sprocket*, which drags the chain around a long steel *guide bar*.

steps.label: Teeth
steps.text: Each sharp *tooth* bites off a chip of wood, and the next one follows right behind it.

steps.label: Oil
steps.text: Oil drips onto the bar so the chain *slides* instead of *overheating*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Rev, grab, *chew*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
